# Template parity fixtures

`native.json` is generated by
`rust/crates/authorizer/examples/template_fixtures.rs` using the pinned native
`cedar-policy` 4.13.0 APIs directly. It does not invoke `cgw_templates` or the
Rust guest operation functions. The shared diagnostic renderer and native source-chain traversal only preserve
upstream error text.

Regenerate after an intentional upstream change:

```bash
cd rust
cargo run --offline --locked --release -p cgw-authorizer --example template_fixtures > ../testdata/parity/templates/native.json
```

Check reproducibility and compare the exported Go API against native results:

```bash
scripts/check-template-parity.sh
```

The fixtures compare resulting policy sets, upstream operation errors,
authorization decisions/reasons, and strict-validation pass/fail. Link arrays
are sorted only for fixture stability; slot and policy semantics come from
Cedar. These cases are regression evidence, not exhaustive or formal proof.
